findings.text: follow-on: the answers paragraph states the choice and score distribution tolerances are both 0.005 per nonzero probability plus 1e-9, but the code at head bounds by the number of offered options (imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3323, tolerance = 0.005 times len(offered) plus 1e-9) and the same fragment's own evidence paragraph already states per-offered; a reader of the answers section takes the retired rule.

follow-on: the plan's section-25 text still mandates that the choice tolerance counts only the criteria that carry a nonzero probability, at 0.005 per nonzero probability, while the code and the evidence fragment now count every offered option; the plan record and the code disagree and the plan was not amended when the bound was reverted.

follow-on: score_worker pairs the full files list against content_decisions, which holds only the successful decisions, with zip strict false; when one content decision fails mid-batch every later file's description is attached to the wrong entry, so a failed file can be described while the last file in the batch is scored with no description. No test exercises a partial failure: the batch-failure test fails both files.
